# Skales

> Websites & systems for service businesses. Builds websites, online booking and follow-up automation for UK service businesses (trades and local operators). Run by Tom Griffiths, one person, in the United Kingdom.

Key facts:
- Builds websites, online booking and follow-up automation for UK service businesses (trades and local operators).
- One person: the person you message is the person who builds it.
- Thirty-six working demonstration builds run live on the site; every business in them is fictional.
- One system a week is built in public on Instagram.
- Clients own their domain, code and accounts from day one; nothing is rented back to them monthly.
- Every build is hand-coded with no page-builder, no theme and no third-party runtime dependencies.
- Contact: thomasrgriffiths08@gmail.com · Instagram @tomxsystems (https://www.instagram.com/tomxsystems/)
- Book a call: https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/book/

## Pages
- [Home](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/): what Skales builds, with a live demonstration build on the page.
- [Work — thirty-six builds](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/): every demonstration build, each running live and each with its own page.
- [Websites](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/websites/): the four kinds of website (loud, motion, quiet, direct) with every example.
- [Tools](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/tools/): the broad tools for any service business and the ones built for a single trade.
- [Services](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/services/): the five services, built as one system — [Websites](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/services/websites/), [Booking and CRM](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/services/booking-and-crm/), [Follow-up automation](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/services/follow-up-automation/), [Meta ads](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/services/meta-ads/), [Google ads](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/services/google-ads/).
- [Automations](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/automations/): [missed-call text-back](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/automations/missed-call-text-back/), [review requests](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/automations/review-requests/), [service reminders](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/automations/service-reminders/), [quote chasing](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/automations/quote-chasing/), [booking deposits](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/automations/booking-deposits/), [on-my-way texts](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/automations/on-my-way-texts/).
- [Try it](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/try/): live demos that run in the browser — a missed call texted back and booked, online booking with a deposit, and a CRM board whose follow-up texts send themselves.
- [Compare](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/compare/): honest comparisons against [a page builder](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/compare/page-builders/), [a monthly trade website](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/compare/trade-website-templates/), [a missed-call app](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/compare/missed-call-apps/), [a directory listing](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/compare/directories/).
- [FAQ](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/faq/): every question in one place, with short answers.
- [Why](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/why/): ownership (clients own domain, code and accounts), one person, built in public, and the FAQ.
- [Book a call](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/book/): four qualifying questions, then a slot straight into the diary.
- [Free teardown](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/teardown.html): three details in, three findings back by message.
- [Notes](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/notes/): short pieces — what a missed call actually costs a service business; why i don’t rent you your own website; thirty-six builds for businesses that don’t exist, on purpose.

## The thirty-six builds

- [Shiftbook](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/shiftbook/): business tool for an invented salon staff rota — Click a cell to place a shift. Clashes flag as you go.
- [Long Exposure](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/long-exposure/): website for an invented long exposure — A film company's site that plays like a film you can scrub.
- [Overhead](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/overhead/): website for an invented overhead — Scroll to climb — the valley draws itself in contours as you rise.

- [Chairside](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/chairside/): business tool for an invented four-chair salon — Rebooks the client at the counter and refills the slots that fall out.
- [Turntable](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/turntable/): business tool for an invented corncrake — The floor, the queue at the door and the deposit rule, on one screen.
- [Roofline](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/roofline/): business tool for an invented ackroyd roofing — A postcode and seven taps draw the roof, then price it.

## Frequently asked
- **Do I actually own the website?** Yes. With Skales the domain, the code and the hosting sit in your own accounts from day one. It is set up so you could walk away tomorrow and lose nothing; that is the whole point.
- **Is there a monthly fee to keep my site online?** No. Skales does not charge a monthly platform fee to keep your own website alive. You pay for hosting and your domain directly, in your own name, at cost. If any quote you get includes a monthly fee to keep your own site online, that is rent.
- **How long does a build take?** A capture website takes days. A full system with booking and follow-up usually takes one to two weeks. You get a date with the quote, and you can watch it being built in public.
- **Are the thirty-six builds on this site real clients?** No, and deliberately so. Every business, person, review and phone number in the demonstration builds is invented, so nothing on this site exposes anyone Skales works with. They are real working software, just for businesses that do not exist.
- **Who actually does the work?** Tom Griffiths. Skales is one person: there is no account manager and no handover to a junior. The person you message is the person who builds it.
- **What kind of businesses is this for?** UK service businesses whose work comes in by phone: plumbers, heating engineers, electricians, roofers, kitchen fitters, landscapers, cleaners, salons and similar trades and local operators.
- **What happens after I book a call or send the form?** Tom Griffiths looks at your website, your Google listing and what happens when someone tries to reach you, then messages you three things: what is leaking, what to fix first, and what it is worth in jobs. If you want it fixed, you get a flat quote. If not, you keep the list.
- **Do you use page-builders or templates?** No. Every build is hand-coded with no page-builder, no theme and no third-party runtime dependencies. Every visual is drawn in code rather than bought from a stock library.

### Four kinds of website. — https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/websites/

Website examples for service businesses | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Work / Websites Four kinds of website. A boxing club and an accountant should not get the same site. The first decision is the lane: how loud, how much moves, how fast it gets to the phone number. Every example is a full website for an invented business, running live. Loud Big, kinetic, confident. The type is the image and one moment does the talking. 3 examples Gyms, bars, studios, events: anyone who needs to be noticed before they are compared. Motion The page is the film: scroll-driven sequences, letterboxes, timecodes, drawn frames. 3 examples Film, video, drone and photography businesses: anyone selling moving pictures. Quiet Plain, calm, expensive. Almost nothing moves; the typography does the work. 3 examples Accountants, clinics, architects, solicitors: businesses whose customers are buying reassurance. Direct Conversion first. One-tap call, a three-field form, the service area, no fluff. 3 examples Trades and local services that live off the phone. When does a business need a loud website? When being remembered matters more than being reassured. A boxing club or a tattoo studio is chosen on feel, so the site moves, the type hits and there is one thing the visitor will describe to a friend. Everything still works: the number, the booking and the address are one tap away. SIGNAL 2027 Website Loud Festival Southpaw Website Loud Boxing club Marrow Pin Website Loud Tattoo studio What does a website for a film or video business look like? Like a film. The visitor scrubs through the work by scrolling, the page carries a timecode, and nothing in it is a stock video: the frames are drawn in code, so the page weighs nothing and plays on a phone. The story reads even if you never scroll. MARÉE — Sel Obscur Website Motion Fragrance house Long Exposure Website Motion Film production company Overhead Website Motion Drone survey filming Why would a business choose a plain website? Because its customers are buying trust, not excitement. A quiet page uses real typography, generous space and one accent, and moves exactly once. It is harder to make than a loud one, because nothing is hiding behind an animation. Atelier Voss Website Quiet Architecture practice Hale Partners Website Quiet Accountant Fern Physio Website Quiet Physiotherapy clinic What does a tradesperson’s website actually need? The number, a form with three fields, proof you cover their street and a reason to ring you rather than the next result. These pages load in a blink, put a call bar under the thumb on a phone and answer the question the customer typed into Google. The only animation is the one that proves a point. You will hear which kind of site your customers actually respond to, and whether you need one at all. ### The tools that run a service business. — https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/tools/

Business tools for trades: 24 live examples | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Work / Tools The tools that run a service business. Software that sits between the customer and the diary. Broad tools fit any business that takes enquiries and books jobs. Specific tools are built around one trade s actual day. Every one runs live with invented data and has a reset inside. Broad Works for any service business: booking, quotes, the pipeline, follow-up, reviews. 13 examples Any business that takes enquiries and puts jobs in a diary. Specific Built around one trade’s actual day: its diary, its paperwork, its reminders. 11 examples One trade at a time: heating, garages, salons, restaurants, roofing, rounds. Which tools work for any service business? The ones that sit between the customer and the diary: taking the booking, chasing the quote, texting back a missed call, asking for the review, keeping every enquiry in one list. Because the gaps between them are where the jobs go missing. An ad that lands on a page that cannot book, a booking that never gets a reminder, a missed call nobody returns. Here the ad points at the website, the website books into the CRM, and the CRM sends the texts, so nothing falls between two suppliers. You can start with one piece and add the rest. Most owners start with the website or the missed-call text-back, because that is where the most work is leaking. The process Teardown, quote, build, handover How does a build work? The teardown. Skales builds websites, online booking and follow-up automation for UK service businesses, and runs Meta and Google ads that send people to them. The aim is one system that turns a search, a tap or a missed call into a booked job. Who is Skales for? Trades and local service businesses whose work comes in by phone, message or search: plumbers and heating engineers, electricians, roofers, builders, cleaners, garages, salons, clinics, and anyone else who books work with customers. Who will I actually deal with? Tom Griffiths. Skales is one person, so the person you message is the person who builds it. How much does it cost? Every job is quoted flat after a short call, and agreed before anything starts. The price depends on how many pages you need, whether you take bookings or deposits, which automations you want and whether you want ads. There are no prices on this site. How long does it take? A website on its own takes days. A full system with booking and follow-up usually takes one to two weeks, built in public so you can watch it being made. Do I own what you build? Yes. The domain, the code and the accounts are set up in your name from day one. Nothing is rented back to you monthly, and if you stopped working with me, everything would keep working. Online booking and CRM for service businesses | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Services / Booking and CRM Booking and a CRM that run the admin for you. Online booking lets customers take a free slot in your diary and pay a deposit to hold it, at any hour, without ringing you. The CRM puts every enquiry, quote and job on one board, and sends the confirmations, chasers and reminders on its own. Book a call Try the demo A missed call, booked in two minutes. A call rings out at 21:47. The system texts back, the customer books and pays a deposit, and the job lands on the board and in the diary. A made-up business, so the numbers are illustrative. Fictional business · illustrative numbers Play the film What you get Booking and CRM What is included? A booking page on your own website, showing only the slots you really have. Deposits taken at booking, for the jobs you choose. Confirmation and reminder texts sent automatically. One board for every enquiry, quote and job, wherever it came from. Quotes chased when they go quiet, on a schedule you set. Invoices and review requests sent when a job is marked done. Where every enquiry came from, so you know which channel books work. No app for your customers to download. It all works in their phone browser. The detail Straight answers How does online booking work? The customer picks the job they need, then a day and a time from the slots you actually have free. Slots that are taken are already gone, so double bookings cannot happen. Where your trade takes a deposit, they pay it by card on the same page. They get a confirmation straight away and a reminder before the day. You get the job in your diary with their details, their notes and the deposit marked paid. What does the CRM actually do? Every enquiry lands on one board, whether it came from your website, a missed call, Google or an ad: Enquiry, Quoted, Booked, Done. Moving a job along sends what should be sent at that stage: the reply, the quote, a chaser if it goes quiet, the confirmation, the reminder, the invoice and the review request. You stop running the business from your text messages, and nothing slips because you were busy. Why take a deposit? A booking with money behind it is a booking people keep. The deposit holds the slot, comes off the final bill, and means the time you have set aside is paid for. You choose which jobs take one and how much. Missed-call text-back sends a text to anyone whose call you could not answer, seconds after it rings out, with a link to book or a quick question. It turns a missed call into a conversation before they ring the next business on Google. Book a call Try the demo Why it matters Missed-call text-back Why does it matter? When you are up a ladder or under a sink, you cannot answer. Plenty of people who reach voicemail do not leave a message; they ring the next number instead. A text back in the first minute keeps them talking to you. How it works Step by step How does missed-call text-back work? The call rings out. You are on a job and cannot pick up. The call goes unanswered, as it would now. The text goes out. Seconds later, the caller gets a text from your business: sorry you missed them, here is a link to book, or reply and you will ring back. They book or reply. They pick a slot on your booking page, or reply with what they need. Either way they have stopped looking elsewhere. You see it all. The missed call, the text and what happened next sit on one card in your CRM, so you know who to ring and who has already booked. The message What the customer gets What does the text say? Sorry I missed your call, I’m on a job. You can book a time here: larchfield.co.uk/book, or reply with what you need and I’ll ring you back. Larchfield Heating An example for Larchfield Heating, a made-up business. Yours is written with you, in your words. What it needs From you What does it need from me? A business number that can forward unanswered calls. Most UK mobile and landline networks can. Your booking link, if you take bookings. If not, the text asks what they need. The numbers you do not want texted, such as suppliers and family. See it run Live demos with a made-up business. You play the customer, then see what the business sees. About a minute each. Numbers you know can be left out, so only new callers get the text. How fast does the text go? Within seconds of the call ringing out, while the caller still has their phone in their hand. Will it spam my customers? No. It only texts people who have just rung you, once, about the call they made. Nobody is added to a marketing list. More in every question, answered . Automated Google review requests | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Automations / Review requests Review requests that go out while the job is fresh. A review request goes to the customer by text when the job is marked done, with one tap straight to your Google review box. Asking every customer at the right moment is how a small business builds its rating without chasing anyone. Book a call Try the demo Why it matters Review requests Why does it matter? Happy customers mean to leave a review and forget. The ones who remember unprompted are often the unhappy ones. Asking everyone, the same day, while they are still pleased with the work, changes who writes your reviews. How it works Step by step How does review requests work? The job is marked done. You move the job to Done in the CRM, or the invoice is paid. The request goes out. A couple of hours later, the customer gets a short text thanking them and asking for a review, with a link that opens your Google review box. One tap to review. They tap, pick the stars and write a line. No searching for your business, no signing in to anything new. You reply. New reviews show up for you to reply to, so every review gets a response in your name. The message What the customer gets What does the text say? Thanks again for having us round today, Priya. No, and it should not. Google does not allow filtering out unhappy customers before asking for a review, so everyone gets asked. A business that does good work comes out of that well. Service reminders that bring customers back | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Automations / Service reminders Service reminders: the work that comes round, booked on its own. Service reminders text your customers when they are due again: the annual boiler service, the MOT, the next haircut, the gutter clean. The work that comes round every year gets booked without anyone having to remember to ring. Book a call Try the demo Why it matters Service reminders Why does it matter? Repeat work is the cheapest work you will ever win, and it is the easiest to lose. Customers do not forget you; they forget the date. Whoever reminds them first gets the job. How it works Step by step How does service reminders work? The job sets the date. When a job that comes round is done (a service, an MOT, a cut), the next due date is worked out and saved with the customer. The reminder goes out. A few weeks before they are due, the customer gets a text saying so, with a link to book. A nudge if needed. If they do not book, one follow-up goes out closer to the date. Then it stops. The diary fills. Bookings from reminders land in your diary like any other, marked as returning customers. The message What the customer gets What does the text say? Hi Sam, your boiler’s due its annual service next month. Book a time that suits you here: larchfield.co.uk/book. Larchfield Heating An example for Larchfield Heating, a made-up business. Usually one, and one follow-up if they do not book. Then it stops until next time. Is it allowed to text past customers? Automatic quote follow-up for trades | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Automations / Quote chasing Quote chasing: no quote goes quiet without a follow-up. Quote chasing sends a friendly follow-up when a quote has not been accepted, a couple of days after it went out, with a link to accept or ask a question. Quotes that go quiet get a nudge without you having to remember who you priced up last Tuesday. Book a call Try the demo Why it matters Quote chasing Why does it matter? Pricing a job takes time, and most quotes are never chased because the person who wrote them is on another job. A customer who has gone quiet is often just busy. The one who follows up politely is the one they book. How it works Step by step How does quote chasing work? The quote goes out. You price the job and send it from the CRM. The customer gets a link to see it and accept it. The system watches. It knows whether they have opened it, and whether they have accepted. The chaser goes out. If the quote is still open after a couple of days, the customer gets a short, friendly follow-up with the link again. Accepted becomes booked. When they accept, the job moves to Booked and the confirmation goes out. If they say no, it is closed and you know. The message What the customer gets What does the text say? Hi Priya, just checking the quote came through OK. Happy to answer any questions, or you can book a date here: larchfield.co.uk/q/4821 An example for Larchfield Heating, a made-up business. Yours is written with you, in your words. What it needs From you What does it need from me? Quotes sent from the CRM, so the system knows when they go out and whether they are accepted. Not one polite message a couple of days later. It reads like a business that cares about the job, and customers often reply to say they had simply not got round to it. How many times does it chase? Once by default, with a second follow-up if you want one. After that the quote is left alone. What if the customer has already accepted? Then no chaser goes. Online booking deposits for service businesses | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Automations / Booking deposits Booking deposits: a booked slot that turns into a job. A booking deposit is a small payment the customer makes when they book online, which holds the slot and comes off the final bill. It turns a booking into a commitment, so the time you set aside is paid for. Book a call Try the demo Why it matters Booking deposits Why does it matter? A no-show costs you the job and the job you turned away to fit them in. A deposit is the simplest fix: a booking with money behind it is a booking people keep, and the ones who cannot make it let you know. How it works Step by step How does booking deposits work? They pick a slot. The customer chooses the job and a free time on your booking page. They pay the deposit. They pay by card on the same page. You choose which jobs take a deposit and how much. The slot is theirs. They get a confirmation with the deposit shown, and a reminder before the day. It comes off the bill. The deposit is taken off the final invoice. Your cancellation rules decide what happens if they cancel late. The message What the customer gets What does the text say? You’re booked: boiler service, Thursday 8 October at 8:00. Your deposit is paid and comes off the final bill. We’ll remind you the day before. Larchfield Heating An example for Larchfield Heating, a made-up business. Yours is written with you, in your words. A small deposit on the booking page is normal for salons, clinics, restaurants and more and more trades. An on-my-way text tells the customer you have set off, with a rough arrival time and who is coming, so they are in, the dog is shut away and the car is off the drive. One tap from the job sheet sends it. Book a call Try the demo Why it matters On-my-way texts Why does it matter? A wasted trip to an empty house costs a morning. A customer who is not sure when you are coming rings to ask, and calls you while you are driving. One text before you set off fixes both. How it works Step by step How does on-my-way texts work? You set off. On the way to the job, you tap On my way on the job sheet on your phone. The text goes out. The customer gets a text with who is coming and a rough arrival time. They get ready. They are in, the parking is clear, and they are not ringing you to ask where you are. Running late is one tap too. If a job overruns, one tap tells the next customer, so nobody is left waiting without knowing why. The message What the customer gets What does the text say? ### Skales vs a page builder — https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/compare/page-builders/

Web designer or Wix? Skales vs page builders | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Compare / Page builders Skales or a page builder like Wix or Squarespace? A page builder is the right choice if you enjoy building, have the evenings to do it, and want a site online for a small monthly fee. A hand-built Skales site is the better choice when the website’s job is to bring in work: it is faster, it books and follows up on its own, and you own it outright. Side by side What A page builder Skales Who builds it You, from a template Me, by hand, for your business How you pay A subscription for as long as the site is live A flat quote for the build, agreed first. Nothing rented back to you Who owns it The platform. Leave, and you usually rebuild from scratch You: the domain, code and accounts are in your name Speed on a phone Depends on the template and the apps you add Hand-coded, with nothing loading that you did not ask for Booking and follow-up Through plans, add-ons or apps, each set up by you Booking, deposits, the CRM and the texts, built in and connected Your time Your evenings and weekends A call and a few messages When a page builder is the better choice You enjoy building and want to do it yourself. The business is very new and you just need something online. The site is a brochure and the work does not come in through it. When Skales is Your work comes in by phone and the site should turn visits into bookings. You want missed calls, quotes and reminders followed up without you. You would rather own the site than rent it. Straight answers The questions people ask Questions people ask Is a page builder cheaper? At the start, usually. Over a few years the subscription and the add-ons add up, and you still do not own the site. Which works out better depends on how long you keep it and what it brings in. Can you move my Wix or Squarespace site? Yes. The content comes across, every old address is redirected to its new page, and the new site replaces the subscription. More in every question, answered . Questions about websites, booking and ads | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / FAQ Every question, answered. Short, straight answers about what Skales builds, what it costs, how long it takes and who owns it, then the questions for each service, automation and comparison. If yours is not here, ask it on a call. The basics Websites Booking and CRM Follow-up automation Meta ads Google ads Missed-call text-back Review requests Service reminders Quote chasing Booking deposits On-my-way texts Skales vs a page builder Skales vs a monthly trade website Skales vs a missed-call app Skales vs a directory listing The basics Start here The basics What does Skales do? Skales builds websites, online booking and follow-up automation for UK service businesses, and runs Meta and Google ads that send people to them. The aim is one system that turns a search, a tap or a missed call into a booked job. Who is Skales for? Trades and local service businesses whose work comes in by phone, message or search: plumbers and heating engineers, electricians, roofers, builders, cleaners, garages, salons, clinics, and anyone else who books work with customers. Who will I actually deal with? Tom Griffiths. Skales is one person, so the person you message is the person who builds it. How much does it cost? Every job is quoted flat after a short call, and agreed before anything starts. The price depends on how many pages you need, whether you take bookings or deposits, which automations you want and whether you want ads. There are no prices on this site. How long does it take? A website on its own takes days. A full system with booking and follow-up usually takes one to two weeks, built in public so you can watch it being made. Do I own what you build? Yes. The domain, the code and the accounts are set up in your name from day one. Nothing is rented back to you monthly, and if you stopped working with me, everything would keep working. Can you guarantee I will rank first on Google? No, and nobody honest can. What a well-built site does is give you the best chance: pages written for what your customers search, proper structured data, a fast site and a consistent Google Business Profile. Searches for your trade in your area are the ones to win first. Are the businesses on this site real? No. Every business, person, review and phone number in the demos and builds on this site is invented, and each one is labelled. They show how the systems work; no client is named or shown. Can I try it before I talk to anyone? Yes. The live demos on the Try it page run in your browser: call a business, book a job, or move a lead across a CRM board, then see what the business sees. Websites The full page Websites How long does a website take? A website on its own takes days. A full system with booking and follow-up usually takes one to two weeks, and you can watch it being built. How much does a website cost? Every job is quoted flat after a short call, because the price depends on how many pages you need, whether you take bookings or deposits, and which automations you want. There are no prices on this site and no monthly fee for a page builder. Do I own the website? Yes. The domain, the code and the accounts are set up in your name from day one. If you stopped working with me tomorrow, the site would keep working. I already have a website. Will I lose my Google ranking if it is rebuilt? Not if it is done properly. Every old address is redirected to its new page, so the links Google already knows keep working, and the new pages are faster and better structured than the old ones. Booking and CRM The full page Booking and CRM Can customers book at night or at weekends? Yes, that is the point. The booking page shows your free slots at any hour, so a customer who finds you at 10pm books then, instead of meaning to ring you in the morning. Can two people book the same slot? No. A slot disappears the moment it is taken, on every device. Do my customers need to download an app? No. Booking, paying the deposit and every text they get works in the browser on their phone. I quote rather than book. Is this still for me? Yes. The CRM board works the same way for quotes: every enquiry gets a reply, every quote gets chased if it goes quiet, and accepted quotes become booked jobs. Can I see where my enquiries come from? Yes. Every enquiry is tagged with where it came from (your website, Google, a missed call, an ad), so you can see which ones turn into booked work. Follow-up automation The full page Follow-up automation What does it cost to run? The setup is quoted flat, like everything else. After that, each text costs a few pence from the text provider. Can I change what the messages say? Yes. Every message is written with you before it goes live, and any of them can be changed or paused with a message to me. Will it text my suppliers or family when I miss their calls? Not if you do not want it to. Numbers you know can be left out, so only new callers get the text. Do I need the website and CRM as well? No, but they work best together. Missed-call text-back and review requests can run on their own; quote chasing and reminders need somewhere to keep the jobs, which is what the CRM is for. Meta ads The full page Meta ads How much should I spend on ads? It depends on your area, your trade and how many jobs you can take on. We agree a test budget on the call, the spend goes to Meta from your own account, and you can change it at any time. Can you guarantee leads? No, and nobody honest can. What you do get is a clear view of what the ads cost and what they booked, so you can decide whether to keep going. Do I need a website first? The ads need a page built to book. If you do not have one, I build it as part of the job, and it carries on working for you whether the ads are running or not. Facebook or Instagram? Both run from one Meta account. Where the budget goes depends on where your customers are, and the tracking shows which one books. Who owns the ad account? You do. It is set up in your name like everything else, so if you stop working with me, the account, the audience data and the history stay with you. Google ads The full page Google ads How much should I spend on Google Ads? It depends on how competitive your trade is in your area and how many jobs you want. We agree a test budget on the call, the spend goes to Google from your own account, and you can change it at any time. How quickly do Google Ads work? Search ads can start showing as soon as Google approves them, so they are the fastest way to appear for searches you are not ranking for yet. Getting the cost per job down takes a few weeks of tuning. Should I do ads or SEO? Usually both. Ads bring enquiries while the website earns its place in the normal results, which takes months. Once the site ranks for a search, you can spend less on ads for it. Can you guarantee the top spot? No. Where an ad appears depends on the budget, the competition and Google. What you get is a clear view of what each booked job cost. Who owns the Google Ads account? You do. It is set up in your name, so the account, the data and the history stay with you. Missed-call text-back The full page Missed-call text-back Does it work with my mobile number? Yes. Your phone forwards calls you do not answer, and the text goes out from there. You keep your number and answer calls exactly as you do now. Will it text suppliers, family or spam callers? Numbers you know can be left out, so only new callers get the text. How fast does the text go? Within seconds of the call ringing out, while the caller still has their phone in their hand. Will it spam my customers? No. It only texts people who have just rung you, once, about the call they made. Nobody is added to a marketing list. Review requests The full page Review requests Can it only ask the happy customers? No, and it should not. Google does not allow filtering out unhappy customers before asking for a review, so everyone gets asked. A business that does good work comes out of that well. When is the best time to ask? The same day, a couple of hours after the job, while the work is fresh and they are still pleased. The timing can be changed for your trade. Does it work for repeat customers? Yes. It can ask once and then leave them alone, so a regular is not asked after every visit. Can I show my reviews on my website? Yes. Real reviews can appear on your site, and once there are enough, in your search results too. Nothing is ever made up. Service reminders The full page Service reminders Which businesses is this for? Any business where the work comes round: boiler services and landlord certificates, MOTs and car services, hair and beauty appointments, window and gutter cleaning, check-ups and maintenance contracts. Can it use my existing customer list? Yes. A spreadsheet with names, numbers and the date of their last job is enough to start. How many reminders does a customer get? Usually one, and one follow-up if they do not book. Then it stops until next time. Is it allowed to text past customers? A reminder about a service they have had before, from a business they used, is the kind of message most customers expect. Anyone who replies to opt out is never texted again. Quote chasing The full page Quote chasing Will customers find it pushy? Not one polite message a couple of days later. It reads like a business that cares about the job, and customers often reply to say they had simply not got round to it. How many times does it chase? Once by default, with a second follow-up if you want one. After that the quote is left alone. What if the customer has already accepted? Then no chaser goes. It only follows up quotes that are still open. Can I still send my own quotes? Yes. You price the job; the system sends it and follows it up. Booking deposits The full page Booking deposits Will a deposit put customers off? A small deposit on the booking page is normal for salons, clinics, restaurants and more and more trades. Customers who are serious about the job pay it; the ones who were never going to turn up tend not to book. Where does the money go? Straight to your own payment account, set up in your name. What if a customer cancels? Your rules decide. Many businesses refund with enough notice and keep the deposit for late cancellations, and the booking page says so before they pay. Can some jobs be booked without a deposit? Yes. You choose which jobs take one, so a free quote visit can be booked without paying anything. On-my-way texts The full page On-my-way texts Does it track my location? No. It sends the text when you tap the button, with the arrival time you choose. Nobody is followed on a map. Can my team use it? Yes. Each person taps from their own job sheet, and the text says who is coming. What about the night before? Every booking already gets a reminder the day before. The on-my-way text is for the morning of the job. Is this only for trades? No. It suits anyone who goes to the customer: cleaners, mobile hairdressers, dog groomers, mechanics, surveyors. Skales vs a page builder The full page Skales vs a page builder Is a page builder cheaper? At the start, usually. Over a few years the subscription and the add-ons add up, and you still do not own the site. Which works out better depends on how long you keep it and what it brings in. ### Own it. Don’t rent it. — https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/why/

Why — one person, built in public, you own it | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Own it. Don t rent it. Skales exists because most service businesses are renting their own website from whoever built it, and getting a brochure for the money. This page is the reasoning, and the straight answers. Ownership Yours from day one Why should you own your own website? You should own your website because it is where your work comes from, and anything that important should not depend on a monthly payment to the person who built it. With Skales, the domain, the code and every account sit in the client s name from the first day. Some builders charge every month, forever, just to keep a site alive. A page-builder account the site cannot leave, a domain registered in the agency s name, a platform fee each one is a lever, and it only gets pulled one way. Every build here is hand-coded, hosted in an account the client controls, with the domain registered to the client. Sack Tom Griffiths tomorrow and everything keeps working. * If a quote includes a monthly platform fee to keep your own site online, that is rent. Walk away. One person No account manager Who builds it? Tom Griffiths does. Skales is one person, based in the United Kingdom, and the person you message is the person who does the work. There is no sales call handed to a junior, and nothing gets lost in a handover because there is not one. Operator Tom Griffiths. Builds every site and system personally. Base United Kingdom. Built for how UK service businesses get work: the phone, Google, word of mouth. Cadence One system a week, built in public on Instagram (@tomxsystems) . Method Hand-coded. No page-builders, no themes, no stock imagery, no third-party runtime. Proof Thirty-six working builds on the Work page , every one open to use. ### What a missed call actually costs a service business — https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/notes/what-a-missed-call-costs/

What a missed call actually costs a service business Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Notes 3 September 2026 Tom Griffiths What a missed call actually costs a service business The sum behind the missed-call text-back, with every assumption on the table — and why the number survives a sceptic. A missed call costs a service business more than the job on the other end of it, because the customer who rang is usually ringing the next firm on the list within the hour. The Stopcock calculator on this site meters that leak from five numbers you already know: calls per week, the share you miss, the value of an average job, how many quotes turn into work, and the share of missed callers who are gone for good. Why the model has a "gone for good" factor Most missed-call calculators quietly assume every missed caller would have booked. They would not. Some ring back, some were price-checking, some booked elsewhere before you saw the voicemail. Stopcock makes that share an explicit slider, so the headline figure is a floor a sceptical owner can defend, not a marketing number. What a text-back in under a minute changes A missed-call text-back sends the customer a message seconds after the ring-out, asks one question, and turns a voicemail into a conversation. The customer who was about to dial the next number replies instead. The follow-up automation on this site does exactly that, and the Redgate demo on the Why page shows the sequence end to end. Open the calculator, put your own numbers in, and argue with it. That is what it is for. ### Why I don’t rent you your own website — https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/notes/why-i-dont-rent-you-your-own-website/

Why I don’t rent you your own website | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Notes 3 September 2026 Tom Griffiths Why I don’t rent you your own website Some builders charge every month, forever, to keep your own site alive. Here is what you own it actually means in practice. A website built by this studio belongs to the business it was built for: the domain, the code and every account sit in the client’s name from the first day. If the client walks away tomorrow, the site keeps working, because nothing about it depends on a monthly payment to the person who built it. What "rent" looks like A monthly platform fee to keep your own site online. A page-builder account the site cannot leave. A domain registered in the agency’s name. Each one is a lever, and the lever only ever gets pulled one way. What ownership looks like Hand-written code with no page-builder and no theme, hosted in an account the client controls, with the domain registered to the client. Every build on the Work page of this site was made that way, and every client build is made the same way. Why do it this way Because the work should be good enough that people stay by choice. Rent is what you charge when you are not sure it is. See the builds Book a call The work Book a call s k ales Websites systems for service businesses. One person, United Kingdom. Thirty-six working builds on this site, every one for an invented business. Thirty-six builds for businesses that don’t exist Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Notes 3 September 2026 Tom Griffiths Thirty-six builds for businesses that don’t exist, on purpose Why every demo on this site is for an invented company, and why that is better proof than a client logo wall. Every one of the thirty-six builds on this site was made for a business that does not exist: Redgate Heating, Northgate Kitchens, Atelier Voss, Fenwick Heating and the rest are invented, and so is every person, review and phone number inside them. That is deliberate. It means nothing on this site exposes a real client’s numbers, customers or setup. Why fictional beats a logo wall A logo wall proves someone paid. A working build proves what was built. Each demo here runs live in the page: you can drag a job across the dispatch board, take a slot in the booking flow, or watch the quote engine price a kitchen. A screenshot of a client site cannot do that, and a client site should not be handed to strangers to click through. What a real build shares with these The approach is identical: hand-coded, no page-builder, no stock imagery, built to do one job for one kind of business, and owned outright by the client.
